headlines.title: 베선트 " 원화 변동성 목격"…엔화 이어 한국도 직접 거론

key_headlines.title: South Korea's Real Estate Tax Overhaul: Acquisition Tax Tied to Housing Units, Property Tax to Price and Residency
key_headlines.summary: The government's tax reform differentiates criteria across real estate taxes, with acquisition and property taxes maintained at current levels while capital gains tax is strengthened to emphasize actual residency from acquisition to sale.

key_headlines.title: Landlords Returning to Primary Residency Trigger Jeonse Crisis and Tenant Hardship
key_headlines.summary: Property owners are abandoning rental plans and returning to primary residency due to rising non-resident owner holding taxes, creating a severe shortage of jeonse (deposit lease) inventory and financial burden on tenants.

key_headlines.title: Seoul's Jeonse and Monthly Rent Prices Soar as Government Plans Housing Supply Expansion
key_headlines.summary: Seoul's average jeonse has reached 700 million won and monthly rent 1.6 million won amid sharp price increases, prompting the government to announce upcoming measures to expand housing supply in the capital region.

key_headlines.title: Morgan Stanley Raises South Korea's 2026 GDP Growth Forecast to 3.4%, Expects Additional Rate Hikes
key_headlines.summary: Morgan Stanley upgraded Korea's growth projection citing strong technology demand and manufacturing recovery, while forecasting the Bank of Korea will accelerate rate increases to 3.5% through Q1 2027.

key_headlines.title: Global EV Battery Market Grows 20% But Chinese Companies Command 72% Market Share
key_headlines.summary: While the global electric vehicle battery market expanded 20% in the first half of 2026, Chinese battery makers consolidated dominance with 72.4% share, pressuring Korean battery manufacturers' market position.

sections.Hot Economy News: South Korea's real estate market is experiencing significant disruption following the government's tax reform announcement. Property owners planning to return to primary residency are abandoning rental strategies, causing a severe jeonse supply shortage and financial hardship for tenants. Seoul's jeonse prices have reached 700 million won while monthly rents approach 1.6 million won, prompting urgent government action. Meanwhile, mid-sized companies showed 8.5% year-on-year export growth in Q1, though the number of exporting companies and export ratio declined slightly, indicating concentrated export performance among larger firms.
sections.Macro & Fiscal Policy: Morgan Stanley raised South Korea's 2026 GDP growth forecast to 3.4%, citing strong technology demand, manufacturing recovery, and growing capital expenditures. The Bank of Korea is expected to implement additional rate hikes in August and accelerate monetary tightening to 3.5% by Q1 2027 as inflation pressures mount from economic recovery. Gyeonggi Province declared a fiscal emergency with a 770 billion won supplementary budget cut, as the province faces revenue constraints with over half its tax revenue dependent on acquisition taxes declining due to real estate market weakness. Cheongju City demonstrated strong economic competitiveness with top rankings in exports (26.52 billion dollars) and employment indicators among major Korean cities.
sections.Financial Markets: The Korean stock market recovered as foreign investors poured in 1 trillion won, with KOSPI rebounding above 6,600 points supported by semiconductor strength and easing AI profitability concerns following strong U.S. tech earnings. The won-dollar exchange rate stabilized around 1,420-1,423 won per dollar amid global oil price stabilization. However, unprecedented market volatility drove approximately 35 trillion won into bank deposits, with major banks' time deposit balances increasing by the largest monthly amount this year as investors sought safer havens. Market participants remain cautious about potential rate hikes from the U.S. Federal Reserve despite recent dovish signals, with CME FedWatch showing 66.5% probability of a September rate increase.
sections.Industry & Technology: The global electric vehicle battery market expanded 20% in the first half of 2026, but Chinese manufacturers consolidated their dominance by capturing 72.4% market share, pressuring Korean battery makers including Samsung SDI and SK Innovation. Hantech, preparing for its KOSDAQ listing, is expanding beyond mobile sensors into electric vehicle battery management systems and data center applications. The semiconductor industry remains volatile due to high sensitivity to global AI chip cycles and concentrated fund flows toward mega-cap stocks like Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix. Multiple new product launches and technology development initiatives signal continued industry competition despite market consolidation trends.
sections.Real Estate: Real estate markets across South Korea face mounting pressure from the government's new tax policies, with jeonse supply dwindling as property owners pursue primary residence strategies to avoid rising holding taxes. Seoul's apartment price appreciation has slowed for two consecutive weeks, though regional disparities persist with Gangnam showing weakness while Joongrang and Nowon districts experience price increases. Busan's real estate market showed resilience with prices rising 0.48% and jeonse index up 3.56%, outperforming other major cities, supported by strong demand in premium residential areas. Multiple civic forums and policy discussions are underway to address housing supply concerns and stabilize the rental market.
sections.International Economy: The U.S. stock market reached record highs with the Dow Jones and Nasdaq gaining amid easing oil prices and expectations of potential Federal Reserve rate cuts in September, though market participants remain cautious about persistent inflation pressures. The Trump administration is actively considering expanding national security tariffs on steel, aluminum, copper, and related products across 14 additional categories as part of its protectionist trade policy. Geopolitical tensions involving China and the Middle East continue to support commodity prices, while the Trump administration undertook emergency central bank lending support for the yen to manage currency markets, raising questions about monetary policy coordination. The Korean won's strength relative to the dollar poses investment challenges for Korean companies, necessitating careful monitoring of exchange rate dynamics.
sections.AI & Economy: Amazon's market capitalization exceeded 3 trillion dollars driven by strong cloud infrastructure growth, as major tech companies begin monetizing AI investments through cloud service tolls and AI computing power rental businesses. SK Telecom reported a 67% increase in Q2 operating profit with AI data center revenue doubling, demonstrating the profitability potential of AI infrastructure investments. The AI data center sector faces approximately 1 trillion dollars in capital expenditure commitments from big tech companies, creating significant financial burdens and potential investment-grade bond market opportunities. The government reported that manufacturing facilities adopting AI achieved average productivity increases of 30% or more and defect rate reductions of 15%, validating AI transformation benefits. SpaceX reported 90% revenue growth in its first earnings release, though investors remain cautious about sustainability of AI-related revenue from excess data center computing capacity rentals.
sections.Others: Denmark is significantly expanding conscription obligations including for royal family members to bolster defense capacity against Russian security threats and U.S. pressure regarding Greenland, with even the second-in-line princess subject to military service requirements. Gwangyang Port Authority continues advocating for operational independence rather than integration with other port authorities, emphasizing its critical role in supporting POSCO's steel exports and the Yeosu National Industrial Complex. Heat waves and surging sterilized milk imports are pressuring domestic dairy producers, with import volumes reaching 24,735 tons in the first half of 2026, up 27.3% year-over-year, threatening Korean milk market viability. SpaceX faces negative free cash flow despite strong revenue growth due to surging AI capital expenditures, illustrating the financial pressures tech companies face while building AI infrastructure.
